subject: PII segmentation & retention exception — follow-up and MA plan draft
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Gomez <sandra.gomez@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PII segmentation & retention exception — follow-up and MA plan draft

Hi Sandra — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the path forward so we have alignment: 

Summary of LumenHealth requirements (as discussed)
- PII segregation: any PHI/PII must not be materialized to persistent logs or embeddings by default.
- 0-retention ask for sensitive routes: Lumen wants an option where raw inputs are not persisted beyond request lifecycle.
- Short retention for operational logs: prefer 24–72 hour TTL on KV/cache and access logs for product telemetry (non-PII).
- Data residency: EU-only residency for datasets related to EU patients; US retention option for US workload.
- Evidence: SOC 2 summary, DPA, and an audit trail for admin actions.

What Redwood proposes as next steps (draft MA plan attached)
1) We’ll share a draft Mutual Action Plan (attached) that lays out timelines for PoC, security review, and legal redlines (attached: MA_Plan_LumenHealth_v1.pdf).
2) Technical PoC: propose a 2-week staging PoC in the eu-central region using our Dedicated/Private route with ephemeral mode enabled for sensitive endpoints.
3) Legal: Kimberly will provide a DPA/Draft SLA and proposed contractual language for a 0-retention exception and admin audit retention.
4) Evidence: attaching a SOC2 summary; we can schedule a deeper evidence pack call with our security team if you need more.

Immediate asks from you: please confirm which endpoints you want classified as "sensitive" for the PoC, and share the list of Lumen admin roles that will need access to logs for the audit review.

I’ve attached the draft MA plan and the SOC2 summary. Ben (cc’d) will follow up with the technical options and an outline for the staging PoC. Kimberly (cc’d) will follow up on DPA/contract language.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marcus Lin

marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock PoC scope: 

1) When you say 0-retention for sensitive routes, does that include:
   - embeddings generated from PHI?
   - debug/trace logs that sometimes capture message fragments?
2) We need clarity on pseudonymization/tokenization options for identifiers in transit — can Redwood perform tokenization at the edge so we never see raw identifiers in the model pipeline?
3) For SOC2 evidence: we’ll need the control mappings for data classification, key management (KMS/HSM), and admin audit log retention policy.
4) DPA: can you provide a draft that includes the exception language for shortened logs and explicit residency controls (EU-only for EU patient data)?

We can do the PoC but want to make sure the default behavior for the PoC reflects the stricter settings (0-retention for PHI, EU region for EU data).

Also copied our security mailing list — they’ll review the MA plan and get back with any high-level redlines.

Best,
Sandra Gomez
Head of Security & Privacy, LumenHealth
Sandra.Gomez@lumenhealth.com

Hi Sandra — looping in some technical detail to answer Marcus’ summary and your questions. Short answers up front, then specifics:

- Embeddings: can be configured to never be persisted for labeled sensitive routes. Our runtime supports ephemeral embeddings and a "no-persist" flag at the model call level.
- Debug/trace logs: we can route traces to an ephemeral buffer and disable persistence for sensitive tracing. Non-sensitive telemetry can be sent to a separate telemetry sink with configurable TTL.
- Tokenization at edge: yes — we support a tokenization proxy that replaces identifiers with reversible tokens before requests enter the model stack. Keys remain under customer KMS when requested.

Detailed options for PoC:
1) Ephemeral mode (sensitive route): raw inputs and embeddings are not written to persistent stores. Request-level KV cache is used for inference only and dropped at request completion.
2) Selective short-retention mode (operational): store non-PII logs/metrics in a separate shard with configurable TTL (24/72/168 hours).
3) Dedicated EU staging: provision a dedicated pool in eu-central with EU-only routing and regional KMS.

Implementation checklist we recommend for the 2-week PoC:
- Week 0: Provision dedicated EU pool, enable tokenization proxy, configure sensitive routes with ephemeral flag.
- Week 1: Ingest sample flows, verify no persisted embeddings, run attack-surface checklist.
- Week 2: Run acceptance tests, handoff to LumenSec for verification.

I’ve added a short technical appendix to the shared MA Plan link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleSharedMAPlan (SEE: "Technical Appendix — PII Segmentation").

If it helps, we can provide a short runbook for your security engineers to validate that no PHI persists.

—

Sandra — thanks for the questions. From a contractual/legal standpoint we can accommodate a narrowly-scoped 0-retention exception with the following guardrails: 

- Scope: the exception will apply only to explicitly-labeled "sensitive" API routes (documented list). All other routes will follow standard retention schedules.
- Evidence & audit: Redwood will supply admin audit logs for operator actions (user provisioning, role changes, access to live sessions). Those audit logs will be retained for 30 days and are not part of the 0-retention exception.
- Tokenization/KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported; when enabled, raw identifiers will be encrypted at rest under the customer key.
- Contractual language: propose adding a DPA clause that lists the sensitive route identifiers and the residency obligation (EU-only handling for specified datasets).

I’ll attach a draft DPA and suggested redline points to the MA Plan (uploaded to the shared Drive). We will also prepare a short DocuSign-ready amendment for the exception if Lumen wants to move forward after the PoC.

DocuSign (draft amendment): https://docusign.example.com/signed/placeholder

Let us know the list of endpoints you want in-scope and any internal audit requirements (e.g., SIEM export, M365 ingestion).

—
Kimberly Park
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
